name: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane wind-radii (storm size) forecasting
description: Fit a model of tropical-cyclone size on the 2004-2014 Atlantic best track and forecast the radius of 34-kt winds in four quadrants 12-72 h ahead for every analysed time of the 2015-2024 storms, given the storm's history and its best-track track and intensity at the verifying times. The score is the mean absolute radius error.

sources.locator: Knaff, Sampson and DeMaria (2007): climatology-and-persistence prediction of tropical-cyclone wind radii driven by the track and intensity forecast.
Knaff et al. (2017): a global statistical-dynamical wind-radii forecast scheme.
Landsea and Franklin (2013): HURDAT2 format, including the four-quadrant wind radii since 2004, and their analysis uncertainty.
HURDAT2 Atlantic best track, release of 4 April 2025 (public domain); the 2004-2024 synoptic records with wind radii are used.

requirements.datasets: Derived from pinned public sources by python3 scripts/prepare_earth.py (hashes in catalog/earth-data-lock.json).

evaluation.benchmark: Earth science: Atlantic hurricane wind-radii (storm size) forecasting
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_radii_model(training_storms) -> model; model.forecast(history, future) -> float array (5, 4) of 34-kt wind radii (n mi) in the NE, SE, SW and NW quadrants at 12, 24, 36, 48 and 72 h. training_storms is a list of the 2004-2014 Atlantic HURDAT2 storms as dicts with numpy arrays time_hours (hours since 2004-01-01 00 UTC), lat (deg N), lon (deg E, west negative), vmax_kt, mslp_hpa (NaN when missing) and r34, r50, r64 ((n, 4) radii in n mi for NE, SE, SW, NW; 0 where the threshold is not reached in a quadrant, NaN when not analysed), plus status (list of HURDAT2 codes) and year, one entry per 6-hourly synoptic record. Forecasts are requested in chronological order from every 6-hourly record of a 2015-2024 storm that is TS, HU or SS with maximum wind >= 34 kt and analysed 34-kt radii and that verifies at one or more leads; history holds that storm's records up to and including the forecast time (same fields); future holds lead_hours, verifies (1 or 0) and the best-track lat, lon, vmax_kt and mslp_hpa at each lead (NaN where the lead does not verify). A lead verifies when the storm is then TS, HU or SS with maximum wind >= 34 kt and analysed 34-kt radii. The candidate runs in a separate sandboxed process (numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and pandas importable; no file, network or subprocess access; one thread) with 120 s of CPU time for fitting and all predictions together; seed any randomness so that results are deterministic. Score: mean over the five leads of the mean absolute error (n mi) over verifying cases and the four quadrants; lower is better. Wrong shapes, NaN or values outside [0, 1000] n mi are invalid

limitations: Best-track wind radii are post-season analyses with large uncertainty (often tens of percent for the 34-kt radii), which bounds the attainable error.

The verifying track, maximum wind and pressure are given (perfect prognosis); operational radii forecasts must use forecast track and intensity, so errors here are smaller than operational ones and not comparable with them.
Only 34-kt radii are scored, at 6-hourly synoptic times; 50- and 64-kt radii and the radius of maximum wind are available as history but not forecast.
A better score is a better statistical storm-size model on these seasons, not a scientific discovery; the held-out observations are public, so search feedback on this split can overfit it.

The candidate runs in a sandboxed child process that receives each case's information only when it is requested, and no statement of the candidate is executed in the evaluator's process; outside macOS (kernel sandbox) deliberately hostile native code could bypass the file policy.

state_of_the_art.statement: No published value exists for this perfect-prognosis protocol. Internal references: persistence of the current radii (the seed) 32.19 n mi; least-squares regression per lead on current radii, intensity change, verifying intensity and latitude, fitted on 2004-2014, 27.88 n mi.

sources.title: Statistical Tropical Cyclone Wind Radii Prediction Using Climatology and Persistence

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the size of a tropical cyclone's wind field (the radii of damaging winds) one to three days ahead.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Wind radii determine the extent of watches and warnings, storm-surge and wave forecasts and the arrival time of tropical-storm-force winds, which sets evacuation timing.

papers.title: Statistical Tropical Cyclone Wind Radii Prediction Using Climatology and Persistence
papers.primary_goal: Forecast tropical-cyclone wind radii statistically from climatology, persistence and the track and intensity forecast.
papers.task_relation: The task scores the same kind of radii forecast at 12-72 h, using best-track instead of forecast track and intensity on the 2015-2024 Atlantic seasons.

papers.title: A Global Statistical-Dynamical Tropical Cyclone Wind Radii Forecast Scheme
papers.primary_goal: Develop and evaluate a global statistical-dynamical scheme for forecasting wind radii.
papers.task_relation: Same forecast target and verification against best-track radii.

science_relevance.reason: Both cited papers have wind-radii forecasting as their main goal, the problem the local task scores; no reproduction of their numbers is claimed.
science_relevance.verification_basis: Crossref metadata checked on 2026-10-10; HURDAT2 radii columns inspected; evaluator run on the pinned release.
